speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; please describe exactly where it is located, how it appeared, and if you have noticed any changes in size, color, or drainage. To help me understand the full picture, do you have any history of diabetes, vascular disease, or recent insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum (likely pathergy-induced by the ant bite in the context of Crohn's disease and diabetes).

Given the history of Crohn's, diabetes, and the rapid progression from a minor trauma (ant bite) to a painful ulcer, I need to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, C-Reactive Protein, and Wound Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up clinical photograph of the ulcer base and borders.
